rules.statement: When a measured value such as cost or usage can't be read (missing file, bad JSON, renamed field, or a run that failed before reporting), don't substitute 0: warn with the source's path and report the value as unknown or as a lower bound.
rules.why: A silent 0 makes a run that spent money look free, and nobody can tell the figure is unknown.
rules.check: Look for catch blocks or fallbacks that set a metric to 0 or a default without a warning. Also look for code that drops a value it did read because a key (such as a session id) is missing, when it could store it under another key.

rules.statement: Give magic numeric constants, such as conversion rates and minimum floors, named variables or constants, and use those names in the expressions instead of bare literals.
rules.why: If the rate or floor changes, someone has to hunt for the numbers inside an expression, and only help text explains what they mean.
rules.check: Look for bare numeric literals with domain meaning inside computed arguments or formulas.

rules.statement: Run a long-lived external CLI or child process with a configurable timeout, kill its process tree when the timeout hits, report the failure, and read its output asynchronously.
rules.why: A session that hangs on a prompt or on the network would otherwise block the run forever, and reading output synchronously can deadlock when the output is large.
rules.check: Look for synchronous invocations of external processes that have no time limit, no kill on timeout, or blocking reads of redirected stdout/stderr.

rules.statement: When code falls back from a dedicated, narrowly scoped credential to a general one (such as GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN or `gh auth token`), warn that the broader credential is in use, recommend a least-privilege token, and document the risk.
rules.why: A general token with broad scopes given to an automated or untrusted-input session can be misused or leaked, when the task needs only narrow access.
rules.check: Look for credential fallback chains that silently pick up general-purpose tokens without a warning or documentation.

rules.statement: In tests, cover the boundary cases of computed limits, such as the minimum floor and the zero/disabled value that passes no limit at all, not only one typical value.
rules.why: A regression in the floor or the zero check would change a spend or resource cap without any test failing.
rules.check: When a diff adds or changes a computed cap, threshold or floor, check whether the tests exercise the floor and the zero/disabled case.

rules.statement: Mention in the CHANGELOG entry or PR description any change that makes an existing check stricter, so that runs that now fail can be explained.
rules.why: Without it, a run that newly fails under the stricter conditions has nothing that explains why.
rules.check: When a diff adds conditions to an existing assertion or validation, check whether the CHANGELOG or PR description mentions them.
